newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine resumes T-bill payments after delay.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine resumes T-bill payments after delay.

text.p: Ukrainian banks began receiving Treasury bill payments from the Finance Ministry several hours late on Thursday, and the central bank chairman promised there would be no more delays.
Representatives of Bank Ukraina and TK Kredit bank said payments for interest and principal on nine- and twelve-month T-bills arrived just after 5 p.m. (1400 GMT).
The ministry's payment to banks of 4.116 trillion karbovanets ($23.3 million) was due on September 18 although the ministry usually effects payments the morning after the due date.
It was the third time in less than a month that the ministry has been late on its payments.

"Today the issue was discussed with the prime minister and it was raised before the president, about the ministry's failure to fulfill its obligations," central bank chairman Viktor Yushchenko told reporters.
"I think that measures have been taken that will guarantee that this issue is closed forever," he said.
Yushchenko did not elaborate on the measures.
A Finance Ministry spokesman said he could not explain the delay.
On August 29, the ministry delayed a $23 million payment for half a day and on September 11 a similar delay occurred with a $22 million payment.
Ukraine has replaced the karbovanets currency with the hryvnia, but some calculations on T-bill transactions are still being conducted in the old currency.
The hryvnia, unchanged at 1.76 to the dollar since its introduction on September 2, equals 100,000 karbovanets. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
